recognize_zh: 周邊血液中多顆中小型淋巴球，核圓或有凹陷（notched／腎形），染色質中度凝集，部分可見小核仁，胞質少到中等且偏深藍、邊緣有時有小突起；這群外觀成熟但核不規則、胞質嗜鹼性的淋巴球增多，符合 T 細胞前淋巴球白血病（T-PLL）。
features: Small to medium-sized lymphoid cells, larger than a small mature lymphocyte
Round to irregular nuclei with notches or indentations; moderately condensed chromatin
Small but visible nucleoli in some cells
Scant to moderate basophilic cytoplasm, occasionally with small cytoplasmic protrusions
Adjacent normal segmented neutrophil for size comparison; red cells without significant abnormalities
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows an increase in small to medium-sized lymphoid cells with round to irregular, notched nuclei, moderately condensed chromatin, small visible nucleoli in a subset, and scant to moderate basophilic cytoplasm that occasionally forms small protrusions. A normal segmented neutrophil is present for comparison, and red cells appear unremarkable. The cells lack the fine blastic chromatin of lymphoblasts. Findings are consistent with T-cell prolymphocytic leukemia, to be confirmed by flow cytometry (mature T-cell phenotype, often CD4+, TdT-negative with TCL1A overexpression) and cytogenetics for inv(14)/t(14;14) or t(X;14).

ddx.vs: Lymphoblasts have fine blastic chromatin and are TdT/CD1a positive, whereas T-PLL cells have more condensed chromatin and a mature TdT-negative phenotype.
Sezary cells have cerebriform grooved nuclei with condensed chromatin and no nucleoli, and occur with erythroderma, lacking TCL1A rearrangement.
ATLL shows multilobated flower cells and is HTLV-1 associated and CD25 positive.
CLL cells are small B cells with block-like clumped chromatin and scant pale cytoplasm, and are CD5+/CD23+/CD19+ rather than T-cell.
